name: LCRS B020551.6-453502 (Hubble)
blurb: LCRS B020551.6-453502, a post-starburst (E+A) spiral galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: gal020750452050-hubble
story: Post-starburst galaxies like this one are among the best candidates for galaxies in transition, turning from gas-rich and star-forming to gas-poor and passively evolving through galaxy mergers. This one is a dusty spiral with two spiral arms, its bulge largely hidden behind dust lanes.

claims.text: The target position (02 07 50, -45 20 50) is the E+A galaxy LCRS B020551.6-453502 (EA19)
Post-starburst (E+A) galaxies are the best candidates for galaxies in transition from gas-rich and star-forming to gas-poor and passively evolving, via galaxy mergers
The E+A galaxies EA06 to EA21 of the Zabludoff et al. (1996) Las Campanas Redshift Survey sample were imaged with Hubble's ACS
EA19 is a spiral (Sab) galaxy with two spiral arms
Dust lanes mask a large portion of EA19's bulge
